title: Simultaneous absolute approximation of an arbitrary qcqs scheme morphism
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $X$ and $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There exist a small nonempty directed partially ordered set $I$, schemes $X_i,S_i$ of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and morphisms $f_i:X_i\to S_i$. The schemes $X_i$ and $S_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $j\geq i$ there are affine transition maps $a_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$ and $b_{ji}:S_j\to S_i$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism], satisfying the identity and composition laws and $f_i a_{ji}=b_{ji}f_j$. There are compatible projections $p_i:X\to X_i$, $q_i:S\to S_i$ with $f_i p_i=q_i f$, such that $X$, with the $p_i$, and $S$, with the $q_i$, are the respective inverse limits in schemes: every compatible family from a test scheme has a unique factorization through the indicated limit. No finite-type hypothesis is imposed on $f$, and the stages $S_i$ are allowed to vary.

source.place: Tag 0GS1, label lemma-approximate-morphism; simultaneous absolute approximation of a morphism (finite-type integer stages are in particular qcqs).

proof.text: Apply [prop-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system] separately to $X$ and $S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] to each resulting small cofiltered system. We obtain nonempty directed sets $A_0,B_0$, schemes $X_a,S_b$ of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, affine transition maps $h_{ca}:X_c\to X_a$ and $g_{db}:S_d\to S_b$ for $c\geq a,d\geq b$ satisfying the identity and composition laws, and limiting cones $p_a:X\to X_a$, $q_b:S\to S_b$. Reindexing retains the stages, their finite-type property and affine transitions. The cited node gives $A_0,B_0$ only as preordered sets, so we replace them by partial orders. Let $A=A_0\times\mathbf N$ with $(a,n)\leq(c,m)$ iff $(a,n)=(c,m)$, or $a\leq c$ and $n<m$. This is reflexive, transitive (if neither relation is an equality, $a\leq c\leq e$ and $n<m<k$), and antisymmetric (two distinct pairs below each other would give $n<m<n$); it is nonempty and directed, $(a,n),(a',n')\leq(c,\max(n,n')+1)$ for any $c\geq a,a'$ in $A_0$. Put $X_{(a,n)}=X_a$, $h_{(c,m)(a,n)}=h_{ca}$ and $p_{(a,n)}=p_a$; the identity and composition laws, affineness and cone compatibility are inherited. The opposite of the order-preserving projection $(a,n)\mapsto a$ is initial in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit]: over $a_0$ lies $(a_0,0)$, and two pairs over $a_0$ have a common upper bound over $a_0$, giving the zigzag $i\leftarrow k\to i'$ of the opposite category, with commuting triangles since $A_0$ is a preorder. Clause (a) of that node shows that $X$ with the $p_{(a,n)}$ is a limit over $A$. Define $B=B_0\times\mathbf N$, $S_{(b,n)}=S_b$, $g$ and $q$ in the same way. From now on $a,c,\dots$ denote elements of $A$ and $b,d,\dots$ elements of $B$; $A$ and $B$ are nonempty directed partially ordered sets.

source.place: Tag 0GS1, lemma-approximate-morphism, first paragraph; Tag 01ZA, proposition-approximate; Categories Tag 0032, lemma-directed-category-system; antisymmetrization by the product with $\mathbf N$ (reviewer repair: the cited reindexing gives a directed preorder) and Categories Tag 002R

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], all $X_a,S_b$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ are Noetherian, hence the stages are quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] they are quasi-separated. Applying [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] to $S_b\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ shows that every $S_b$ is locally of finite presentation over this common base. Thus the source stages are qcqs and the target stages have the precise presentation hypothesis needed below.

source.place: Tag 0GS1, second paragraph, hypotheses for Tag 01ZC; supporting Tags 01T6, 01OY and 01TX

proof.text: For every $b\in B$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-map-limit-factorization] over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ to $q_b f:X\to S_b$ and $X=\varprojlim_aX_a$. It gives $a\in A$ and $u:X_a\to S_b$ with $up_a=q_bf$. Whenever an additional lower bound $a_0\in A$ is prescribed, choose $c\geq a,a_0$ and replace $u$ by $uh_{ca}$; then $uh_{ca}p_c=q_bf$. Thus a factorization exists for every target stage, with source index above any prescribed source bound.

source.place: Tag 0GS1, second paragraph: factor the composite to each target stage by Tag 01ZC

proof.text: Let $I=\{(a,b,u)\mid a\in A,\ b\in B,\ u:X_a\to S_b,\ up_a=q_bf\}$. This is a small set: it is a subset of the disjoint union of the morphism sets $\operatorname{Hom}(X_a,S_b)$ over the small set $A\times B$. It is nonempty by step 3. Define $(c,d,v)\geq(a,b,u)$ to mean $c\geq a$, $d\geq b$, and $g_{db}v=uh_{ca}$. The identity and composition laws for $g,h$ prove reflexivity and transitivity. If two triples dominate each other, antisymmetry of $A,B$ gives identical indices; the displayed equation then gives identical maps, so this order is antisymmetric.

source.place: Tag 0GS1, third paragraph: the set of triples and its displayed order

proof.text: To prove directedness, take $i=(a,b,u)$ and $i'=(a',b',u')$. Choose $d\geq b,b'$ in $B$, and use step 3 to choose $e$ and $v:X_e\to S_d$ with $vp_e=q_df$. Choose $c\geq a,a',e$. The two maps $uh_{ca},g_{db}vh_{ce}:X_c\to S_b$ become equal after $p_c$, since both composites equal $q_bf$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-finite-type-limit-map-equality] to obtain $c_1\geq c$ where they agree. Apply the same node at $c_1$ to $u' h_{c_1a'},g_{db'}vh_{c_1e}:X_{c_1}\to S_{b'}$, whose composites with $p_{c_1}$ both equal $q_{b'}f$, obtaining $c_2\geq c_1$. The first equality persists by precomposition. Consequently $(c_2,d,vh_{c_2e})$ is in $I$ and dominates both original triples. Both applications use the original qcqs source system over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and the locally finite type targets $S_b,S_{b'}$; neither assumes any finite-type property of $f$. Choosing an upper target stage $d$ repairs the lower-target comparison in the printed proof, which alone cannot give an upper bound in $I$.

source.place: Tag 0GS1, third paragraph, directedness argument, with its target-index direction repaired using Tag 01ZC injectivity

proof.text: The order-preserving projections $r:I\to A$ and $s:I\to B$ are cofinal in the following explicit sense. For any $a_0$, step 3, using any $b\in B$, gives a triple with $r(i)\geq a_0$. For any $b_0$, it gives a triple with $s(i)=b_0$. For two triples whose $r$-indices are at least $a_0$, their common upper bound from step 5 also has $r$-index at least $a_0$. Thus the opposite projection $I^{op}\to A^{op}$ meets both initial-functor conditions: an object over each $a_0$, and the length-two zigzag $i\leftarrow k\to i'$ over $a_0$. Exactly the same argument applies to $I^{op}\to B^{op}$, with $b_0$ replacing $a_0$. All triangle compatibilities hold because these are poset categories.

source.place: Tag 0GS1, third paragraph, cofinality of both projections; Categories definition-initial

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit] to these two initial functors and the original limiting cones. Its cone-restriction assertion gives $X=\varprojlim_{i\in I}X_{r(i)}$ with projections $p_{r(i)}$, and $S=\varprojlim_{i\in I}S_{s(i)}$ with projections $q_{s(i)}$. In particular, these are limits in schemes, with the required unique factorization for compatible maps from every test scheme.

source.place: Tag 0GS1, final paragraph; Categories Tag 002R, lemma-initial

proof.text: For $i=(a,b,u)$ put $X_i=X_a$, $S_i=S_b$, $f_i=u$, $p_i=p_a$, $q_i=q_b$. For $j=(c,d,v)\geq i$ put $a_{ji}=h_{ca}$, $b_{ji}=g_{db}$. The definition of the order gives $f_i a_{ji}=b_{ji}f_j$; membership in $I$ gives $f_ip_i=q_if$. The transition identities, compositions, affineness and projection compatibilities are those of the original systems. The finite-type and qcqs properties were verified in steps 1 and 2, and both limit properties in step 7. This supplies every asserted clause while allowing the target stages to vary.
